Kavita: The shop assistant told me the dress doesn't come in my size, but they can order it in a week.
Naina: Did you leave a deposit?
Kavita: No, they said I only pay when I come to pick it up.

When does Kavita have to pay for the dress?
She has to pay when she comes to pick it up.

Packet label: Roasted peanuts, lightly salted. Net weight 200 grams. Best before six months from packing. Keep in an airtight container after opening. Packed in a unit that also handles sesame, so may contain traces of sesame. Please read the label before giving it to young children.

What might the peanuts contain traces of?
They may contain traces of sesame.

Cycling club note: We will ride to the lake on Sunday. Meet at the park gate at 6 am. Helmets are a must. The ride is twelve kilometres each way, and we will rest at the banyan tree halfway. Bring a bottle of water. Slow riders will go in front.

Where will the riders rest?
They will rest at the banyan tree halfway.

Termites build mounds that can be taller than a person. Inside, small tunnels let air move through the mound and keep the temperature steady. Workers carry soil bit by bit, and each mound can be home to millions of termites.

What do the tunnels inside a termite mound do?
They let air move through and keep the temperature steady.

Coal is found in layers under the ground. In India it is mined in states like Jharkhand and Odisha. Miners work in large open pits or go down shafts, and the coal is then carried by train to power stations.

What do power stations make by burning coal?
The text doesn't say, but power stations burn coal to make electricity.

Flamingos are pink because of what they eat. The tiny shrimp and algae in their food contain a colour that the birds' bodies turn into pink. Chicks are born grey and become pink only after they eat this food for some time.

Why are flamingos pink?
The colour comes from the tiny shrimp and algae they eat.

Sea turtles return to the beach where they were born to lay their eggs. A mother digs a hole in the sand, lays her eggs and covers them before going back to the sea. The warmth of the sand decides how fast the eggs grow, and the babies hatch at night.

When do the baby sea turtles hatch?
They hatch at night.

A procession carrying a decorated chariot moves through the old town of Puri each summer. Thousands of people take hold of the ropes and pull it along. The streets are lined with food sellers and singers. Drummers walk beside it, and the crowd claps and chants as the ropes are pulled.

What is a chariot?
The text doesn't say, but a chariot is a light vehicle with two wheels, pulled by horses or people.

The painting in the hall of the village council shows a boat on a wide river at sunset. It hangs above the fireplace and has a dark wooden frame. Nobody remembers when it was hung there. Visitors often stop to admire the soft colours of the sky. The council keeps the hall locked on weekdays.

Who painted the picture?
The text doesn't say, and I don't know who painted it. A local art teacher or the council records might help.

A group of musicians plays at the corner of Market Road on Saturday evenings. They have a harmonium, a pair of drums and a bamboo flute. People stop to listen and put coins in a bowl. Sometimes a young woman sings with them, and the sweet seller next door turns his radio off when they begin.

Question: What is a harmonium?
The text doesn't say, but a harmonium is a keyboard instrument that makes sound with air pumped through reeds.

A street musician in Prague played the violin near the old bridge every afternoon. A little girl stopped to listen each day on her way home from school. One afternoon she brought a coin from her own pocket and dropped it in his hat. He bowed and played her favourite song.

What did the little girl put in the musician's hat?
She put in a coin from her own pocket.

What did Pia and her father do each morning?

The family rented a small cottage near a lake in the Swiss mountains. Each morning, Pia and her father rowed a boat to the middle of the water to watch the sun come over the peaks. On the last day, the lake was so still that the mountains looked upside down in it.
They rowed a boat to the middle of the lake to watch the sun come over the peaks.

The river near the village was calm in summer and loud in the rains. Last August it rose so high that it covered the footbridge. The villagers walked a long way around by the road until the water went down, and the children were allowed to stay home from school for two days.

What did the children get when the river covered the bridge?
They were allowed to stay home from school for two days.

In the school canteen, Mrs Pinto served idli every Wednesday with coconut chutney and a spicy sambar. Karan always asked for extra chutney. One day she ran out, so she mixed a spoonful of curd with salt and green chilli and gave him that instead. He said it was even better.

What did Mrs Pinto give Karan when the chutney ran out?
She gave him a mix of curd, salt and green chilli.

Looking after a fish tank: feed the fish a small pinch of food once a day. Remove any food they have not eaten after five minutes. Change one quarter of the water each week using water left in a bucket overnight. Keep the tank out of direct sunlight.

How do fish breathe?
The text doesn't say, but fish breathe using gills, which take oxygen from the water.

Reminder: Monday is the last day to return library books before the exams. After that, a fine of one rupee a day will be charged. Students can drop the books in the box at the office. Please check that your name is written inside the cover.

What is a fine?
The text doesn't say, but a fine is money you must pay as a punishment for breaking a rule.

The school's lost-and-found box held a purse with some coins yesterday. The class teacher announced it in assembly. Aman said it was his, described the colour, and received it back. The box is kept near the school office door, and the clerk checks it every evening.

Why is it important to return lost items?
The text doesn't say, but returning lost items is honest and kind, and it helps the owner get their things back.

A Chennai author will read from her children's book at the library next Saturday at 11 am. Children may ask her questions afterwards. Signed copies will be available at the counter, and tea will be served for parents. The library is on Temple Road, beside the post office, and the reading room is open to all.

Where can signed copies be bought?
Signed copies will be available at the counter.

Notice: due to heavy rain, the lake path is closed until further notice. Visitors can still use the garden path and the picnic area. The park staff will put up a sign when the lake path reopens. The lake is the park's most popular spot, and many families walk there on weekends.

Which paths can visitors still use?
Visitors can still use the garden path and the picnic area.

A new magazine for kids, Little Stars, is now in the library. It has riddles, a comic strip and a short story in each issue. Students can read it in the reading corner but cannot take it home. New issues arrive on the first of each month.

What is a riddle?
The text doesn't say, but a riddle is a puzzling question with a clever answer.
